sections.content:
You know from Unit 24 that pronouns attach to the end of an affirmative command (*dímelo*). With an infinitive or a gerund, you have two equally correct choices for pronoun placement:

1. Before the conjugated auxiliary verb:
• 'Te lo voy a decir.' / 'Te lo estoy diciendo.'

2. Attached to the infinitive or gerund:
• 'Voy a decírtelo.' / 'Estoy diciéndotelo.'

items.spanish: No te preocupes, mañana voy a devolvértelo.
items.english: Don't worry, tomorrow I'm going to return it to you.

items.spanish: Carlos está buscándolo en su mochila.
items.english: Carlos is looking for it in his backpack.

sections.content: Notice the written accent: the stress stays where it was, so two pronouns on an infinitive (dar + se + lo = dárselo) and even one pronoun on a gerund (buscando + lo = buscándolo) need a written accent mark.
